2008A16.goal: A small circle sits in the $60^\circ$ sector $AOB$, tangent to both radii and internally tangent to the big circle (radius $R$). We want the area ratio, i.e. $\left(\tfrac rR\right)^2$. Its centre lies on the bisector of the angle.

tools.name: Distance to the sides
tools.why: The centre is at distance $d$ from $O$ along the bisector, which makes $30^\circ$ with each side.

tools.name: Internal tangency
tools.why: The circles touch on the far side along the bisector.

2008A16.approach: $r=\tfrac d2$, so $d=2r$. Then $R=d+r=3r$ and the ratio is $\tfrac19$.

steps.title: Centre distance
steps.explain: The radius to a tangent point is perpendicular to $OA$; with the $30^\circ$ angle, $r=\tfrac d2$.

check.q: A point at distance $d$ from $O$ on the bisector of a $60^\circ$ angle is how far from each side?

steps.title: Ratio
steps.explain: $R=2r+r=3r$, so the areas are in ratio $\tfrac19$.

2008A16.bridge: Express $R$ in terms of $r$ using the bisector.
2008A16.shortcut: For a sector of angle $2\theta$: $\tfrac rR=\tfrac{\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}$; here $\tfrac{1/2}{3/2}=\tfrac13$.
2008A16.recognize: Circle inscribed in a sector: centre on the bisector, distance from $O$ is $r/\sin(\text{half-angle})$.

2008A17.goal: We want the area of all points outside an equilateral triangle (side $6$) within distance $3$ of it. This band is three rectangles on the sides plus round corners.

tools.name: Band along a side
tools.why: Points whose nearest point is on that side.

tools.name: Corner sectors
tools.why: The three corner pieces together make one full circle of radius $3$.

2008A17.approach: Three rectangles $6\times3$ give $54$. At each vertex a sector of radius $3$ fills the gap; their angles are the exterior angles, totalling $360^\circ$, so together they are a full circle: $9\pi$.

check.q: What is the area of the band along one side?

steps.title: Sectors
steps.explain: Each sector has angle $360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ$; three of them make $360^\circ$, area $9\pi$.

check.q: What is the angle of each corner sector?

2008A17.bridge: Rectangles on sides plus one full circle at the corners.
2008A17.shortcut: For any convex shape: band area $=\text{perimeter}\times r+\pi r^2$.
2008A17.recognize: Points within $r$ of a convex polygon (outside it): perimeter times $r$ plus a full circle.

2008A19.goal: Rectangle $PQRS$ ($PQ=2$, $QR=6$) is rotated $90^\circ$ about $R$, then $90^\circ$ about the new $S$. We want the length of $P$'s path: two quarter-circle arcs.

tools.name: Arc length
tools.why: A $90^\circ$ rotation moves a point along a quarter circle.

tools.name: Distances in a rectangle
tools.why: The radius is the distance from $P$ to the centre of rotation.

2008A19.approach: First rotation: radius $PR=\sqrt{40}=2\sqrt{10}$. Second: radius $PS=6$ (distances are preserved by the first rotation).

check.q: What is the diagonal of a $2\times6$ rectangle?
What is a quarter circle's length with radius $6$?

2008A19.bridge: Each rotation contributes a quarter circle with radius = distance from $P$ to the pivot.
2008A19.shortcut: Rotations preserve distances inside the rectangle, so just use the original $PR$ and $PS$.
2008A19.recognize: Rolling or pivoting shapes: each pivot gives an arc whose radius is the distance to the pivot.

2008A20.goal: Trapezoid with bases $AB=9$, $DC=12$, diagonals meeting at $K$, and $[AKD]=24$. We want the area. The diagonals cut each other in ratio $9:12=3:4$.

tools.name: Same height
tools.why: Triangles sharing a vertex and a line of bases.

2008A20.bridge: Scale $24$ by $\tfrac34$ and $\tfrac43$, double the side triangle.
2008A20.shortcut: With base ratio $a:b$ and side triangle $S$: total $=S\cdot\tfrac{(a+b)^2}{ab}=24\cdot\tfrac{441}{108}=98$.
2008A20.recognize: Trapezoid diagonals: four triangles with areas $a^2,ab,ab,b^2$ (scaled).

2008A21.goal: A plane through opposite cube vertices $A,C$ and midpoints $B,D$ of two opposite edges cuts a quadrilateral. We want its area. It is a rhombus, so use its diagonals.

tools.name: Coordinates
tools.why: $B,D$ are midpoints of opposite vertical edges not touching $A,C$.

tools.name: Rhombus area
tools.why: All sides equal and diagonals perpendicular.

2008A21.approach: All four sides are $\sqrt{1+\tfrac14}=\tfrac{\sqrt5}2$, so $ABCD$ is a rhombus. Diagonals: $AC=\sqrt3$ (space diagonal), $BD=\sqrt2$.

check.q: What is the length of a unit cube's space diagonal?

2008A21.bridge: Rhombus: half the product of the diagonals.
solution: Every side is $\tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}$, so $ABCD$ is a rhombus.
2008A21.shortcut: $BD$ is a face-diagonal-length segment parallel to a face diagonal, so it's $\sqrt2$ without coordinates.
traps: Treating it as a square of side $\tfrac{\sqrt5}2$ ($\tfrac54$).
2008A21.recognize: Cross-sections through opposite cube vertices: often rhombi; find the diagonals.

2008A22.goal: Starting at $6$, each step is $2x-1$ (heads) or $\tfrac x2-1$ (tails). We want $P(\text{fourth term is an integer})$. Only $3$ flips, so draw the tree.

tools.name: Integers stay integers under heads
tools.why: Once a term is a fraction, can it recover? $2\cdot4.5-1=8$, yes. So compute every path.

2008A22.shortcut: Small trees: just enumerate; don't hunt for a pattern.
traps: Assuming a non-integer term stays non-integer.
2008A22.recognize: Few random steps with simple rules: enumerate the tree.

2008A23.goal: Two subsets of $\{a,b,c,d,e\}$ with union $S$ and intersection of size exactly $2$, unordered. Each element is in both, only the first, or only the second.

tools.name: Element-by-element choices
tools.why: The union is $S$, so every element is somewhere.

tools.name: Unordered pairs
tools.why: The two subsets are never equal here.

2008A23.approach: Choose the $2$ shared elements: $\binom52=10$. Each of the other $3$ goes to exactly one subset: $2^3=8$. Ordered: $80$; unordered: $40$.

check.q: In how many ways can $3$ elements each be put into exactly one of two sets?

steps.title: Unordered
steps.explain: The two sets always differ (three elements are in only one of them), so each pair is counted twice: $40$.

2008A23.bridge: Pick the overlap, distribute the rest, halve.
2008A23.shortcut: $\binom52\cdot2^{3-1}=40$: fix which set gets one particular remaining element.
2008A23.recognize: Pairs of sets with conditions on union/intersection: decide each element's status.

2008A24.goal: $k=2008^2+2^{2008}$; we want the units digit of $k^2+2^k$. Find $k\bmod10$ for $k^2$ and $k\bmod4$ for $2^k$.
2008A24.approach: $2008^2$ ends in $4$; $2^{2008}$ ends in $6$ ($2008\equiv0\pmod4$). So $k$ ends in $0$ and $k^2$ ends in $0$. $k\equiv0\pmod4$, so $2^k$ ends in $6$.

check.q: What is the units digit of $2^{2008}$?

steps.title: Units digit of $2^k$
steps.explain: $k$ is divisible by $4$, so $2^k$ ends in $6$. Total $0+6=6$.

check.q: If $4\mid n$, what is the units digit of $2^n$ ($n>0$)?

2008A24.shortcut: Units digits of $2^n$ cycle with period $4$; always reduce the exponent mod $4$.
2008A24.recognize: Units digit of a tower: work mod $10$ for the base and mod $4$ for the exponent.

2008A25.goal: Six $1\times x$ mats on a round table of radius $4$: each mat's outer side of length $x$ is a chord of the table, and adjacent mats share inner corners. We want $x$. The inner sides form a regular hexagon of side $x$.

tools.name: Regular hexagon
tools.why: The distance from the centre to a side of a regular hexagon with side $x$.

tools.name: Chord condition
tools.why: An outer corner lies on the table's edge.

2008A25.approach: Each mat's outer side is parallel to its inner side, $1$ farther out: at distance $\tfrac{\sqrt3}2x+1$ from the centre. Its endpoints are $\tfrac x2$ to either side, on the circle.
2008A25.bridge: Inner corners make a hexagon; the outer corner is on the circle.
solution: Inner sides form a regular hexagon of side $x$, apothem $\tfrac{\sqrt3}2x$.
2008A25.recognize: Symmetric arrangements of $n$ pieces around a circle: the inner corners form a regular $n$-gon.
